request: In the Welder Quals sheet (Welder ID, Name, Process, Expiry Date) highlight the whole row red if the qualification expired before today and yellow if it expires in the next 60 days. Clear old highlights first so it can be run again. Tell me how many rows are highlighted.

In the BOM sheet (Part No, Description, Required Qty, Unit) write Check in a Flag column for every row where Required Qty is blank, not a number, zero or negative, and clear the Flag on the other rows. Add the Flag heading if it isn't there. Tell me how many rows I flagged.

In the GRN sheet (GRN No, Part No, Received Qty, Received Date, Inspector) highlight the GRN No cell yellow when the Inspector is blank, and write Future date in the Remark column when Received Date is after today. Clear old highlights and old remarks first. Tell me how many rows have a yellow GRN No.

From the NCR Register (NCR No, Category, Issue Date, Status) build a Category Summary sheet with, for each category, how many NCRs are Open and how many are Closed, categories in alphabetical order. Rows with no category are ignored.

From the weld log (Weld Seam No, Welder ID, Weld Date, Joint Type) count the welds per joint type and write the counts on a Joint Summary sheet, the biggest count first. Ignore rows with no joint type.

From the Dispatch sheet (Dispatch No, Customer, Planned Date, Actual Date) make a Customer Summary sheet with the number of dispatches per customer and how many of them were late (Actual Date after Planned Date). Customers A to Z.

Compare the BOM (Part No, Required Qty) with the GRN (Part No, Received Qty). In the BOM add a Received column with the total received per part, summing the GRN lines, and a Balance column with received minus required. Add the headings if they are missing.

Check the NDE Report (Weld Seam No, Result) against the Weld Log (Weld Seam No, Visual). List on a Not Inspected sheet every weld log seam whose Visual is Accepted but which has no row in the NDE Report. Seam numbers can have stray spaces.

Check the Consumable Issue log (Issue No, Batch No, Qty Issued, Job ID) against the Job Tracker (Job ID, Status). In the issue log write Closed job in a Remark column for every issue whose job is Closed, and clear the remark on the others. Tell me how many issues are for closed jobs.
In the GRN sheet trim the spaces from the Part No and GRN No cells and make the Part No upper case. Change nothing else, and tell me how many cells changed.
In the weld log delete every row where both Weld Seam No and Welder ID are blank (leftover empty rows) but keep any row that has at least one of them. Tell me how many rows I deleted.
In the NCR Register remove duplicate NCR No rows, keeping the first one, and tell me how many I removed. NCR numbers can differ in upper and lower case.

In the Calibration Tracker (Instrument ID, Next Calibration Due) write Date? in the Next Calibration Due cell when it holds text instead of a real date, and leave real dates and blank cells alone. Tell me how many cells I marked.
Read the text of the file status.txt in the Job Folder (a folder path I give the macro) and write it in cell B1 of the Jobs sheet. If the file isn't there, write the word Missing in B1 instead.
In the Stock sheet (Batch No, Qty On Hand, Unit Cost, Value) put a formula in the Value column for every data row: Qty On Hand times Unit Cost. Excel 2016 only.
Add a sheet called BOM Copy to the workbook with a copy of the BOM sheet, but only if there is no sheet called BOM Copy yet. Running it twice must not add a second one.
On the NCR Register find the row of NCR number NCR-104 and write Reviewed in its Status column. Return the row number, or 0 if that NCR isn't there.

A monthly weld quality tool, started with one macro. (1) In the Weld Log (Weld Seam No, Welder ID, Weld Date, Process, Visual, Remark) write Not qualified in Remark for welds whose welder has no row for that process in Welder Quals (Welder ID, Process, Expiry Date), or whose qualification expired before the weld date; clear Remark on the others. (2) Copy every weld whose Visual isn't Accepted or whose Remark is Not qualified to an Exceptions sheet with the same headings. (3) On a Welder Summary sheet write each welder's welds, exceptions and exception rate. (4) On a Month Summary sheet write the totals: welds, exceptions and rate. The output sheets are rebuilt every run.

A receiving check tool, started with one macro. (1) In the GRN (GRN No, Part No, Heat No, Received Qty) write Check in a Remark column when Received Qty is not a positive number or Heat No is blank, and clear Remark on the others. (2) On a Missing Certs sheet list the GRN lines whose Heat No isn't in Material Certs (Heat No, MTC No). (3) On a Shortages sheet list each BOM (Part No, Required Qty) part whose total of the valid GRN quantities is below the required quantity, with the shortfall. (4) On a Receiving Summary sheet write the number of Check lines, missing certs and short parts. The output sheets are rebuilt every run.

A weekly QA report tool, started with one macro. (1) On an Overdue NCRs sheet list the Open NCRs older than 30 days from the NCR Register (NCR No, Issue Date, Status, ITP No). (2) In the ITP Tracker (ITP No, Point, Inspection Status) write NCR Hold in a Hold Flag column for every point that has an Open NCR against its ITP No, and clear it on the others. (3) On a Calibration Due sheet list the instruments (Instrument ID, Next Calibration Due) that are overdue or due within 15 days. (4) On a QA Summary sheet write the number of overdue NCRs, held ITP points and instruments due, with labels. The output sheets are rebuilt every run.
